title: Tech Stock Sell-Off: Down 13%, Is Microsoft a Buy Now?
summary: Tech stocks have been hit hard this month as investors worry about the enormous amount of money being spent on artificial intelligence (AI), and Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) has been no exception. Shares are down about 13% from their all-time highs. But I think Microsoft is being unfairly punished here. While many big tech companies are free cash flow negative due to heavy AI spending, Microsoft has affirmed it will remain in the black at least through fiscal 2027. Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue » That's a big deal. And I think it's one reason why the tech sell-off in November presents an attractive buying opportunity for Microsoft before the end of 2026. Microsoft is one of the biggest players in the cloud computing space, holding 21% of the global cloud infrastructure market. That makes Azure the second-largest provider of cloud services behind Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN). In Microsoft's fiscal first quarter of 2027, which ended Sept. 30, Azure revenue increased 48% from the previous year. Total Microsoft Cloud revenue was $63.9 billion, up 30% from a year ago, and the company's commercial backlog reached $677 billion. That's an enormous amount of business coming down the line, so Microsoft is spending freely to ensure it has enough computing capacity to meet demand. It spent $45.2 billion on capex in the quarter. But even with that spending, free cash flow remained positive at $18.6 billion. That's because Microsoft generated $58 billion in operating cash flow during the quarter, up 29% from a year earlier. That's a big difference from some other tech companies whose AI spending has pushed free cash flow into negative territory. Despite concerns about AI spending , Microsoft's underlying business is performing very well, thanks to its well-known software business. Nearly 4 million companies use Microsoft 365, including its popular office programs such as Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook. Those subscriptions provide recurring revenue, while Microsoft's Copilot AI products provide opportunities to sell more services to existing customers. Microsoft 365 commercial cloud revenue increased 17% during the quarter. That helped Microsoft's fiscal first-quarter revenue increase 19% to $92.3 billion, while operating income climbed 21% to $45.9 billion.…

title: Microsoft Copilot AI Predicts a Very Interesting BTC Move: Up or Down?
summary: Bitcoin’s next major rally might not come from another ETF approval, a familiar institutional purchase, or even a change in Federal Reserve policy. Instead, Microsoft Copilot AI predicts a development that fundamentally changes how the world’s largest economy views digital assets. Copilot imagines a coordinated government-backed Bitcoin acquisition program that transforms BTC from a speculative investment into a strategic national reserve asset. ( SOURCE: Microsoft Copilot AI Predicts a Huge BTC Reversal ) It sounds ambitious, perhaps even fanciful, but the foundations for such a development are already being laid. With sentiment near rock bottom, conditions for an extraordinary countertrend rally could be more favorable than many investors realize. Copilot’s optimistic outlook comes as the entire crypto market saw a slight overnight recovery, with total market cap up +2% to $2.15 trillion, while Bitcoin surged +2.4% to reclaim $60,000. Market Cap 24h 7d 30d 1y All Time Bitcoin’s recent performance has been difficult to defend. Deteriorating macroeconomic conditions, institutional outflows, geopolitical uncertainty, and the fallout from October’s devastating Binance security incident have weighed heavily on investor confidence. BTC has fallen below $60,000, while November has threatened to become its worst monthly performance since June 2022. The prevailing narrative is increasingly pessimistic, with some investors questioning whether the current cycle has already peaked. However, extreme pessimism can also create opportunities. Markets rarely reverse when everyone is comfortable, and Bitcoin has historically staged aggressive recoveries when positioning becomes excessively defensive. The important distinction is that bearish sentiment does not necessarily mean bearish fundamentals. Beneath the recent price weakness, institutional adoption continues to develop, while several longer-term catalysts remain intact.
